gen-megrim-gf-cal-sans: Angular and a bit sci-fi. Megrim keeps every stroke at one measured thickness, while Cal Sans runs a single friendly stroke width with a tall x-height, so the two feel built from the same stubborn logic.
gen-megrim-gf-carlito: Futuristic and angular, Megrim draws every stroke as one unbroken line. Megrim is best when it draws big, monoline shapes, while Carlito's plain sans build keeps open round letters clear at small sizes.
gen-megrim-gf-changa: Changa reads clean, its lowercase standing tall like cast iron capitals. Megrim's futuristic angles keep horizontals and verticals matched in thickness, while the sans below brings real muscle to every line of text.
gen-megrim-gf-courier-prime: Precise and structured, Courier Prime fills most of its height with lowercase. Courier Prime keeps a drafting-pen line moving through generous round mouths, so text under Megrim feels steady, paragraph after paragraph.
gen-megrim-gf-days-one: Days One reads approachable, with an x-height that fills the whole line. Megrim's futuristic strokes show a rope-like consistency in every stem, bowl and tail, and the sans below keeps that rhythm going.
gen-megrim-gf-epunda-sans: Megrim is best at headline drama, angular and futuristic, with a pipe-like body to every stroke. But Epunda Sans does its best work as plain sans text, with oversized counters and curves holding plenty of daylight.
gen-megrim-gf-farro: Megrim holds every stroke to one measured thickness, which gives its angular letters a futuristic edge. And Farro, with no stroke contrast at all and compressed ascenders, makes the whole pairing feel approachable and uncomplicated.
gen-megrim-gf-fragment-mono: Megrim sketches angular, futuristic letters with every stroke ending at a measured thickness. Fragment Mono lays letters out like nails on a ruler, so long stretches read steadily, with no stroke contrast to slow the eye.
gen-megrim-gf-geist-mono: Geist Mono sets fixed-width, code-style letters with big side gaps and lowercase that rises high. And Megrim's angular, futuristic strokes make that monospace body feel like part of a technical drawing.
gen-megrim-gf-genos: Megrim's curves never thin at the shoulders, so its angular, futuristic letters hold one measured thickness from stroke to stroke. Genos keeps tight spacing and a smooth, snag-free read, the pair's best trait.
